extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutional applicants seeking NIDA/NIH grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: Index of NIDA funding mechanisms, priorities, programs, and supplemental applicant resources (NOF/FAQs/webinars) to guide researchers in finding and preparing grant and cooperative agreement applications to NIDA/NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Research Priorities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level programmatic priorities that guide NIDA funding decisions; serves as subject-area guidance for applicants about topics of interest to the Institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Funding Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of NIDA’s strategy for funding, based on programmatic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how NIDA aligns funding decisions with programmatic priorities; useful for applicants to understand strategic emphases when developing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Special Interest (NOSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Special Interest (NOSI) - Formerly known as Drug Abuse Topics of Special/Continuing Interest (DAT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism used to highlight specific research topics of interest; applicants should consult NOSIs to identify targeted areas where NIDA encourages applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Advisory Council on Drug Abuse (NACDA) Approved Concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: National Advisory Council on Drug Abuse (NACDA) Approved Concepts – The purpose, scope, and objectives of approved concepts for potential funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes approved concepts that may lead to future funding opportunity announcements (FOAs); useful for planning responsive research and anticipating future NOFOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Challenges Program
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDA Challenges Program – Crowd-sourced opportunities for providing solutions for particular goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive challenge/prize mechanisms for soliciting innovative solutions; applicants should follow challenge-specific rules and deliverables rather than standard grant formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for Research Training and Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for Research Training and Career Development – Grant funding opportunities for research training and career development at institutions across the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training and career-development award mechanisms (e.g., K, T, F, diversity supplements); applicants should consult specific FOAs for eligibility, allowable costs, and required components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helping to End Addiction Long-term (HEAL) Initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Helping to End Addiction Long-term (HEAL) Initiative – Congressional initiative to address the opioid overdose crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large, priority research initiative with its own RFAs, NOFOs, and supplemental programs; applicants should review HEAL-specific guidance and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA International Program
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDA International Program – International research collaboration opportunities on drug abuse and addiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities and mechanisms to support international collaborations; applicants should follow international eligibility rules and partnership requirements in relevant NOFOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Grants & Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: See NIDA’s Resources for Grants & Contracts to learn more about applying for a grant and the pre-approval and approval process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central resource for application processes, policies, pre-award and post-award procedures, and contacts; applicants should consult these resources for procedural requirements and institutional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Supplements for Grants & Cooperative Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Supplements for Grants & Cooperative Agreements – Additional funding to an active NIDA grant or cooperative agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to request supplemental funds to an existing award for new or expanded activities (e.g., diversity supplements, urgent competitive revisions); applicants must follow supplement-specific instructions and eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Opportunities Update: Finding NIH NOFOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in fiscal year 2026, NIH will no longer post notices of funding opportunities in the NIH Guide; to find NIH notices of funding opportunities please explore the NIH Grant Opportunities search tool which links to grants.gov, NIH’s single official source for grant and cooperative agreement funding opportunities. (NIH announcement NOT-OD-25-143.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural change affecting where applicants locate NOFOs; applicants must use the NIH Grant Opportunities search tool / grants.gov for official funding announcements going forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Funding App retirement notice
rubrics_metrics.description: As of October 2025, the NIDA Funding App has been retired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not rely on the retired app and must use the NIH/Grants.gov search tools and NIDA webpages for up-to-date funding information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Information for NOFOs and Related FAQs/Webinars (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Information for NOFOs — lists webinars, FAQs, and supplemental guidance for specific FOAs and topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides targeted pre-application webinars, FAQs, and clarifying notices for specific RFAs/NOFOs. Examples listed on the page include: Pre-Application Virtual Presentation for TranSINDA (RFA-DA-25-037 & RFA-DA-25-038); Supplemental Information for NOT-DA-22-064 (NIH Brain Development Cohorts Biospecimen Access); FAQs for Avenir Award Program (RFA-DA-24-007, RFA-DA-23-014); FAQs for Registry of Medical Cannabis Use and Health Outcomes (RFA-DA-23-011); Supplemental Information for NIH Developmental Studies Biospecimen Access Program; Pre-Application Webinar for PAR-21-183 (Developing Digital Therapeutics for SUDs); FAQs re: Establishment of a Standard THC Unit (NOT-DA-21-049); FAQs re: NOSI administrative supplements for COVID-19 research (NOT-DA-21-041); RFA-DA-21-009 pre-application webinar and FAQs (ENDS interventions); Step Up for SUD: Drug Target Initiative (RFA-DA-20-025); FAQs for Avenir Award (Genetics/Epigenetics DP1); FAQs for NOT-DA-19-003 (HEAL initiative supplements); Supplemental FAQs for NIDA Research E-cigarette PAR-17-156; Supplemental FAQs for RFA-DA-17-014 and RFA-DA-17-023. Applicants should consult the specific supplemental item for details on eligibility, application components, deadlines, and clarifications.
